RF coupling into EEG front ends is shown on hardware by a 2023 peer-reviewed workshop paper already in the catalogue (C80) and, independently, by a 2026 preprint that injects RF noise into three commercial headsets for privacy. The status change rests mainly on the 2023 evidence, not on new 2025 or 2026 attack results.
Two of three source strings cannot be tied to a publication on this technique.

A peer-reviewed 2025 study reports membership inference against EEG CNN classifiers by a limited-knowledge adversary (dataset level). A 2026 preprint found membership inference weak (AUC 0.50 to 0.70) on EEG foundation-model embeddings, so the effect depends on model and setting.

Digital, dataset-level attacks on EEG biometric models are now reported in a peer-reviewed letter and a preprint. Evidence is mixed: motor-imagery authentication resisted the black-box attack and the resting-state weakness exists without any attack. No physical presentation attack on a live EEG authenticator was found. If the status vocabulary requires hardware or live-system evidence, keep EMERGING.

Neuronal Flooding and Neuronal Jamming are evaluated in the same in-silico studies (IEEE Access 2020, C107; Neurocomputing 2025), yet QIF-T0025 is DEMONSTRATED and QIF-T0026 is THEORETICAL. The two should carry the same status and both should say simulation only. No implant, animal or human demonstration was found.

Two 2025 papers model manipulation of closed-loop neural systems in simulation (false data injection on a DBS sensor link; adversarial perturbation of EEG in a cognitive feedback loop on public datasets). Neither involves a device or participant. Weak evidence; a change is optional.
